quote: “Had Aristotle prepared victuals, he would have written more.”
source: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz, Reply to Sor Filotea de la Cruz, the philosophies of the kitchen (trans. Margaret Sayers Peden, 1982)
note: Trimmed to the sentence confirmed in Peden’s translation, first published in A Woman of Genius (1982) and reprinted in Poems, Protest, and a Dream (Penguin, 1997). The proposed lead-in clause about trivial details could not be checked against the edition, so it is left out.

evidence.where: Peden’s wording confirmed in the Los Angeles Review of Books essay on Sor Juana and in search summaries citing Poems, Protest, and a Dream (Penguin Classics); the 1982 Lime Rock Press edition itself was not opened
evidence.edition: A Woman of Genius: The Intellectual Autobiography of Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz, trans. Margaret Sayers Peden, Lime Rock Press, 1982; reprinted in Poems, Protest, and a Dream, Penguin, 1997
evidence.locator: Respuesta a Sor Filotea, the passage on the philosophies of the kitchen (the egg observations)

reason: The line is real and Peden’s, but only the final sentence could be confirmed verbatim in her wording; the lead-in clause is left off rather than shipped unconfirmed. Not shipped, not at cap, not banned.
